The Asian Development Bank–Japan Scholarship Program funds about 300 students each year from ADB developing member countries to study approved master's (and in some cases doctoral) programmes, mostly in economics, management, health, education, agriculture, environment and technology. There is no central application deadline: candidates apply directly to a participating university, which forwards eligible files to ADB, and applications should reach the university at least six months before the intended start.

Programme Highlights

  • Roughly 300 scholarships per year funded by the Government of Japan through ADB
  • Apply directly to participating universities — each sets its own closing date
  • Full package: tuition, stipend, housing allowance, insurance and travel
  • Work requirement: two years of full-time professional experience after the first degree

Who Should Apply

Nationals of ADB developing member countries with a bachelor's degree, at least two years of work experience, and admission to an approved programme; return-to-home-country commitment applies.

Funding and Costs

Full scholarship: tuition, monthly subsistence and housing allowance, books, medical insurance and travel for approved programmes.

Deadline and How to Apply

Shortlist participating universities (in Japan and across the region), check each one's ADB-JSP page for its deadline, and apply at least six months ahead of your start date. Key deadline information: No central deadline — apply through a participating university at least six months before your intended start.
